llm.summary: The skill's code largely matches its stated purpose (monitor conversations and run mock hearings), but its automated task instructions allow reading arbitrary file paths and writing results with no path validation — a scope that could be abused to access sensitive files, so caution is warranted.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim an AI courtroom that watches conversations and runs hearings; the included code implements pattern matching on message history, creates verdict objects, conducts LLM-driven deliberation, and stores results under ~/.openclaw/courtroom — all consistent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md documents an Automated Task mode that says the agent will "Read the specified file" and "Write the verdict to the specified output file." The code also accepts a file path argument and unconditionally reads/parses the file. There is no explicit path restriction or validation in the instructions or the shown code, which means an automated trigger could cause the skill to read arbitrary filesystem locations (e.g., sensitive files) and write outputs — increasing the risk of inadvertent data access or exfiltration. The SKILL.md also contains the prompt-injection phrase 'ignore previous instructions' (used in detection rules), which the pre-scan flagged.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no remote downloads; the skill is instruction-only with bundled JS source. No external packages are pulled at install time. This lowers supply-chain risk compared to arbitrary downloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. It uses the user's HOME (process.env.HOME) to create ~/.openclaw/courtroom for logs/verdicts — reasonable for a local tool. No unrelated secrets or cloud credentials are requested.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Metadata indicates autonomy (skill may run automatically) and the source comments state it auto-initializes to monitor conversations. Autonomy is the platform default, but combined with the unvalidated file-read/write behavior in automated mode this increases the potential blast radius. 'always' is false, so it won't be force-included in every run, which mitigates some risk.

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- The skill generally does what it says: it inspects conversation history, detects behavioral patterns, runs a judge+juror deliberation using the agent LLM, and writes verdict files under ~/.openclaw/courtroom.
- Automated mode: SKILL.md and the code say the skill will "read the specified file" and "write the verdict to the specified output file" for automated task messages. There is no path validation shown. Before enabling automated triggers or giving the skill autonomy, ensure automated task inputs are restricted to trusted conversation files; otherwise a crafted message could cause the skill to read arbitrary files on disk.
- Autonomy: the skill can invoke the model (agent.llm.call) to perform deliberation. Autonomous invocation plus file I/O increases the risk surface — consider disabling autonomous execution or gating automated triggers until you audit the code and test in a sandbox.
- Review code paths: inspect the full skill.js and courtroom.js (the provided listing appears truncated in places) to confirm there are no hidden network calls, remote endpoints, or unexpected exec/spawn usage. Verify file write locations and logging behavior if you must keep recorded verdicts.
- Mitigations: run the skill in a restricted environment (limited filesystem permissions), require signed/whitelisted automated tasks, or request the author add explicit path whitelisting and input validation. If you lack the expertise to audit the code, avoid enabling automated/autonomous modes and prefer manual runs on known conversation files.
